Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 3 days of watery diarrhea, crampy left lower abdominal pain, transient vomiting and subjective fever; currently able to tolerate fluids but has been fatigued and going to work despite symptoms.
- Clinical impression: likely acute gastroenteritis (probably viral; bacterial possible). Conservative management recommended with oral rehydration, symptomatic treatment, and short sick leave; return if no improvement in 3–4 days or sooner if worsening.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute diarrheal illness/gastroenteritis.
  - Timeline: symptoms started ~3 days ago; loose watery stools 6–7 times/day; vomiting at onset but has stopped; subjective fever at symptom onset; currently weak and lethargic.
  - Symptoms: crampy, intermittent lower abdominal pain localized to the left side; anorexia; able to hold down fluids; no blood in stool or vomit.
  - Exposures: ate takeaway/Chinese restaurant meal ~4 days ago; one child in household had vomiting but no diarrhea.
  - Systems review / pertinent negatives: no ongoing fever recorded, no sweating/night sweats reported, no back pain, no other bowel disease history.
  - Examination: no physical exam findings documented (examination was not performed).
  - Differential: viral gastroenteritis most likely; possible bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis.
  - Management given: oral rehydration (Dioralyte recommended), paracetamol advised for fever/weakness (two tablets up to four times daily recommended by clinician), advised conservative care (no antibiotics currently), advised 2–3 days off work to rest.
  - Follow-up: return if symptoms not improved in 3–4 days; consideration of stool testing if ongoing symptoms.

Issue 2:
- Asthma (chronic, background).
  - Status: patient reports asthma is controlled with use of an inhaler.
  - Medications: inhaler in use (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - No acute asthma exacerbation documented during this visit.

Issue 3:
- Occupational impact / work restriction.
  - Patient is an accountant and has been attending work despite symptoms; clinician recommended taking 2–3 days off work to allow recovery and reduce symptom burden.
  - No formal sick note text recorded in transcript.

Medications:
- Inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol — recommended by clinician: "two tablets up to four times a day" (tablet strength not documented).
- Dioralyte (oral rehydration solution) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other regular medications reported.

Allergies:
- No allergies mentioned in the consult.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (controlled with inhaler).
- No other past medical history reported.

Social History:
- Lives with wife and two children.
- Occupation: accountant; has been working during illness.
- Smoking: denies smoking.
- Alcohol: denies alcohol use.

Preventative History:
- No preventative care or screening history documented (cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, bone density, vaccinations, optometry, skin checks not mentioned).

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs recorded.
- No physical examination documented; clinician stated plan to examine but did not document findings.

Plan:
- Conservative management for presumed gastroenteritis:
  - Oral rehydration (Dioralyte recommended) and maintain fluid intake; light foods as tolerated.
  - Paracetamol for fever/feeling unwell as advised by clinician.
  - Avoid antibiotics at this stage.
- Occupational advice: take 2–3 days off work to rest and recover.
- Follow-up: review if symptoms persist or worsen; return in 3–4 days if not improving.
  - If ongoing symptoms, consider stool sample testing and further investigations.
- Safety netting: seek earlier review if worsening, high fever, severe dehydration, blood in stool, or inability to tolerate fluids.

Document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate) recorded.
  - No physical examination findings documented despite clinician indicating intent to examine.
  - No documented allergy status explicitly confirmed.
  - No medication names/doses fully documented for inhaler or ORS; paracetamol tablet strength not provided.
  - No formal sick certificate text or return-to-work note documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient reported subjective fever at symptom onset but did not provide a measured temperature; no objective temperature is documented.
- Transcript quality:
  - Transcript is generally clear and intelligible; minimal conversational filler.
